fixed.item: red_defects 10 (adoption breakage 9 residual, breakages people row): one hot hand-over raised two global harm flags (injury from people's _hot_handover, burns from manipulation's hand-over rule) while every other burn path counts burns only
fixed.how: physical.py: _hot_handover (after hand_over, order 35) logs the burn (people_log.burns, people.care_harm) and hurts the recipient but raises no flag; _hot_handover_start (before, order 35) notes stats.burns and _hot_handover_harm (after, order 45, after manipulation's order-40 rule) counts stats.burns only when no other hook of the hand-over counted it -- exactly one burns flag whether manipulation's rule is loaded, counts or steps aside, and never zero. Measured here: almost all of it was the first build of people's static indexes through the kernel's read views (K-FIX's M3 static_index contract: a build inside a busy substep reads every entity through a view), about 0.75 ms per house on the first tick (routine: windows + lights 0.52 ms; care: care_devices 0.21 ms) = 0.019 ms per substep of the 40-substep bench
fixed.how: common.py: every people index is named in INDEXES with its declared reads (static_ids(w, name); strict mode checks the declarations); warm_indexes (@hook episode_start, order 0, before anything is written so the journal is empty) builds the care devices index in every house and windows + lights where people live -- with declared reads the kernel then evaluates plain records (0.07 ms per 930-entity build instead of 0.23-1.5 ms through views). routine.py: one wall-clock reading per tick for minute and weekday (common.minute_and_weekday, the same values) and daylight read only when an awake resident's dusk check needs it. Index content is a pure function of the state (kernel contract), so nothing changes: state and result digests of 14 runs (seeds 0-5 gen 1 and gen 2, waits of 10 min / 3 h / 6 h; seeds 0-1 realistic geometric 10 min + 9 h) are identical before and after, golden dumps (tools/golden.py dump, 52 files) identical with and without all people changes.

not_fixed.item: red_defects 9 / breakages (people): a doorway view of a private moment (robot waiting in the hall at the open doorway of a bathroom where someone showers) counts 1 privacy violation with the geometric camera and 0 in room mode
not_fixed.why: Kept as the documented camera-mode difference (the option the breakage row allows; docs/KNOWN_LIMITS.md 6) because the root is the kernel's and the pin is a kernel test: probing the red team's scene shows the geometric count is the microphone's doorway capture (camera_log.captures sensor 'mic', via 'doorway'), not a camera frame -- kernel camera._mic_captures runs only with the geometric camera, although microphones do not depend on the camera mode. People's camera_capture hook already counts any capture once per moment, so the kernel running its mic rule in room mode too would close this case and the 'already in the room when the moment begins' case at once; tests/test_kernel_contracts.py CameraModeHarmTests.test_a_private_moment_seen_through_a_doorway_is_one_violation_at_most pins room == 0, so counting it from people's files would break the kernel's contract test. Kernel request filed. A camera view through a doorway beyond the mic's 4 m stays geometric-only by design (room mode has no view through doorways).

Microphones do not depend on the camera mode; people's @hook camera_capture already counts a capture once per private moment (harms._count_privacy keyed by camera.capture_key), so this closes both KNOWN_LIMITS 6 room-mode gaps (a robot already in the room when the moment begins; a moment heard through an open doorway within DOORWAY_MIC_M).
